initiatives.name: I Will Go Strategic Plan 2025–2030

aims.text: The I Will Go strategic plan has a far-reaching vision that seeks to align resources with measurable goals and expects all church entities and church members to implement their own action plans.

All Seventh-day Adventists are committed to faithfully fulfilling the sacred purpose to reach the world and are connected to Christ’s Advent movement that is global in scope, yet local in strategic implementation.
The strategic plan’s measurable goals are aligned under four priorities: Communion with God, Identity in Christ, Unity through the Holy Spirit, and Mission for All.
1.1 Time spent in daily unrushed prayer, Bible study, and meditation on the life of Christ and biblical themes
1.2 Daily family worship participation
1.3 Daily usage of the Sabbath School Bible study guides for all ages
1.4 Weekly participation in prayer meetings or small groups
1.5 Weekly reading of Ellen G. White’s writings
1.6 Weekly worship attendance at Sabbath School and church services
1.7 Practicing the stewardship principles of time, talents, tithe, offerings, and health
2.1 Acceptance and practice of Bible-based, Christ-centered beliefs with special emphases on the church’s characteristic and unique doctrines, which point to a loving, gracious God
2.2 Understanding, experiencing, and sharing of the joy of forgiveness (justification) and holiness (sanctification) through the power (righteousness) of Christ
2.3 Understanding and practice of a biblically based wholistic lifestyle that expresses our relationship with Christ and invites all others to God’s abundant life
2.4 Knowledge and affirmation of Adventist identity and the Lord’s leading throughout Adventist history
3.1 Church members embracing worldwide church unity in the body of Christ through biblical truth as understood by Seventh-day Adventists, led by the Holy Spirit
3.2 Cooperative working relationships across church, organizational, and institutional boundaries/structures to advance mission

3.3 Community and harmony in local churches and in church organizations at all levels of church structure, through the power of the Holy Spirit and training in biblical reconciliation and conflict resolution

3.4 Commitment to zero tolerance of physical, emotional, spiritual, and sexual abuse through regular review of policies, background checks where possible, and clear and prompt action to deal with abuse
3.5 Cross-cultural appreciation, respect, mission to, and care for all people groups, including the poor, the vulnerable, and people with disabilities
4.1 The number of church members sharing the gospel and making disciples
4.2 The work of spiritual nurture and evangelistic training after baptism so that new believers become part of Total Member Involvement in the mission of Christ
4.3 New groups of Seventh-day Adventist believers worldwide, particularly in urban areas, in the 10/40 Window, and among Post-Christians
4.4 Mission by young people and to young people
4.5 Mission engagement by all church entities through promoting wholistic health, humanitarian care, education, and outreach to displaced persons
4.6 The use of traditional and new media to proclaim the Three Angels’ Messages and connect people to Adventist worshiping groups

localChurch: The plan expects every church entity and member to implement their own action plan: set the church’s yearly plan under the four priorities (Communion with God, Identity in Christ, Unity through the Holy Spirit, Mission for All).

Use the 22 measurable goals (each worded “significant increases in …”) as the checklist for the church plan, e.g. 1.2 daily family worship, 1.4 weekly prayer meetings or small groups, 4.1 members sharing the gospel, 4.2 training new members after baptism, 4.4 mission by and to young people.
Present the plan to the congregation with the ready-made social media templates, PowerPoint presentations and print materials at iwillgo.org.
Expect to be measured by member surveys: the plan says most goals will be measured by surveys of church members during 2025–2030.

initiatives.name: OneVoice27: Mission for All (public theme “All Things New: Hope Starts Here”)

aims.text: The presenters outlined a coordinated emphasis for September 2027 in which the Seventh-day Adventist Church will proclaim the gospel “to every nation, tribe, tongue, and people” through a unified message and an integrated use of media.

OneVoice27 is designed to connect large-scale media outreach with on-the-ground engagement by local congregations so that interest generated online and on air leads to Bible study and membership pathways.
a worldwide evangelism initiative designed to bring together media outreach, local churches, and members in a global effort to share the gospel in September 2027.

OneVoice27 calls the Adventist Church to spiritual preparation, unity, member involvement, and mission. It brings the church together — every member, every congregation, moving forward with one voice.
the General Conference is focusing on two primary objectives: equipping members and reaching seekers.

localChurch: Use the free Global Launch Sabbath kit from the GC Ministerial Association (order of service, sample sermons, slides, bookmark). The launch Sabbath was 5 Sept 2026, but the kit can still be used to start late.

Commissioning Card: during the altar call every member writes one name (a person God has put on their heart) and one first step for this week (a visit, a call, an invitation, a helping hand or a message).

Build a prayer movement with the OneVoice27 Prayer Journal (personal devotion, prayer groups, church-wide prayer). Join the Ten Days of Prayer (6–16 Jan 2027), the “prayer launch pad” for OneVoice27, and the 40-day prayer initiative (23 Jul–31 Aug 2027).

Prepare members spiritually by praying, studying Daniel and Revelation, and reading The Desire of Ages daily. A special edition, Jesus: The Desire of Ages, with a six-month daily reading plan is planned.
Train a media ministry team with “Clicks to Digital Evangelism” and the shorter OneVoice27 Digital Evangelism Guidebook. Encourage members to share content on their own social media.
Connect online interest to the church: Adventist World Radio’s Global Bible School is presented as the tool to receive and follow up interests through local churches.

Members can take part by sharing content, forming small groups, studying the Bible with others and building relationships in their community. Members who are not online can still serve neighbours in person.
Plan public proclamation and harvest events for September 2027. Each division and union adapts the plan to its own setting, so check the NAD research file for NAD-specific plans.

The General Conference is working to revitalize Ellen White’s concept of Centers of Influence and to establish a network of self-sustaining "Life Hope Centers" in key urban areas around the world.

These centers feature a wide variety of activities such as lifestyle education, treatment rooms, bookstores, reading rooms, restaurants, literature ministry, lectures, small groups, instruction on preparing wholesome food, and more.
Life Hope Centers are an integrated evangelistic outreach. They provide an opportunity for lay people to be involved in ministry using their unique gifts.

initiatives.name: All Things New — the NAD’s public expression of the global OneVoice27 initiative

aims.text: Through OneVoice27, the NAD is looking to mobilize members, churches, schools, ministries, conferences, and unions around a shared mission focus leading to September 2027.

The global initiative seeks to unite the Seventh-day Adventist Church in a prayerful, coordinated, and contextualized effort to share the story of Jesus and the gospel message through personal witness, local outreach, and media ministries.
Pray Like Jesus will focus on spiritual renewal through prayer, Bible study, and reading The Desire of Ages.
Serve Like Jesus will encourage churches and members to engage in acts of compassion and community service that reflect Christ’s love.

Share Jesus will mobilize members to distribute the sharing book; participate in personal witnessing, including sharing their faith in digital spaces; and engage in coordinated outreach efforts across North America.
Follow Jesus will focus on discipleship, spiritual growth, Bible studies, and helping individuals take next steps in their faith journey.
It is designed to help individuals grow spiritually, help congregations serve their communities, strengthen digital and personal witness, and build clear pathways toward baptism and discipleship.

localChurch: Introduce it to the church board with the free All Things New overview presentation (English, Spanish or French).
Start members on a Desire of Ages reading plan: 1 chapter a day or 5 pages a day from Sept. 5, 2026, or 1 chapter a day from January 2027.

Plan the year in the four overlapping phases: Pray Like Jesus (Sept. 2026 – Mar. 2027), Serve Like Jesus (Jan. – Aug. 2027), Share Jesus (Apr. – Sept. 2027), public events in September 2027, Follow Jesus (Oct. – Dec. 2027).

Give out the special sharing book (nine chapters of The Desire of Ages, produced by Pacific Press; the NAD goal is five million copies) to neighbours, coworkers, family and people met through community service.

Run a church-based social media campaign with the shared Digital Media Library (posts, reels, short films, videos); point people who respond to the dedicated digital platform for prayer, Bible studies and connection to a local church.
Show and share the short film “When Hope Shows Up” (English and Spanish), and sign up for the All Things New newsletter.

initiatives.name: Pentecost & Beyond

aims.text: Pentecost & Beyond is a movement inviting every Seventh-day Adventist church member in North America to share the gospel.

Inspired by the power and unity of the early church in Acts 2, it challenges believers to move beyond a single event into a lifestyle of mission—living out their faith through prayer, evangelism, and intentional discipleship.
Pentecost & Beyond is a movement inviting Seventh-day Adventists in North America to collectively hold proclamation events throughout the year 2026.
The Pentecost and Beyond initiative has four areas of focus: Prayer, community engagement, proclamation events, and discipleship.
This movement is designed to continue indefinitely — as an ongoing rhythm and focus for the church — until Jesus comes again.

localChurch: Pray first: start or join a church prayer group and sign up for the monthly Pentecost & Beyond newsletter, which lists the churches and schools to pray for each month.
Engage the community before the series: felt-needs seminars, food pantries, literature distribution, health seminars, sports or family events, Bible studies.
Hold a proclamation event — an evangelistic series, in-person or online Bible study groups, or a health-and-Bible event — and pace it with the 90-Day Plan.
Disciple new believers with Bible studies, small groups and social activities.

Use the free resource lists (prayer, community engagement, proclamation, discipleship, school evangelism) and the recorded training webinars; a small church without a preacher should contact its conference for help.
Optional giving: AdventistGiving → World Offerings → “Pentecost and Beyond”. Note: the FAQ says no Pentecost 2025 funding is being given out now; gifts go to future evangelism initiatives.

initiatives.name: Atlantic Union Strategic Plan 2025–2030: Evangelism & Church Growth (theme “United We Go to Grow God’s Kingdom”)
